title: Post-Impressionism
description: Bold color and expressive form — the bridge from Impressionism to modern art.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.medium: Oil on artist's board, mounted on cradled panel
items.description_narrative: This self-portrait by Vincent van Gogh, painted in 1887, captures the artist with characteristic intensity. Utilizing bold brushstrokes and vibrant colors, the work exemplifies his innovative approach to portraiture during his Parisian period.
items.tags: self-portrait, post-impressionism, oil painting, expressive, dutch art, portraiture, intense
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: The Poet's Garden
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's 'The Poet's Garden' vividly portrays a sun-drenched park landscape, painted during his productive period in Arles. With its expressive brushwork and vibrant palette, the artwork reflects the artist's intense engagement with nature and color.
items.tags: garden, landscape, arles, post-impressionism, vibrant, expressive, oil painting
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: A Peasant Woman Digging in Front of Her Cottage
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh depicts a solitary peasant woman toiling in the soil outside her humble dwelling, rendered with earthy tones and somber realism. This early work showcases his profound empathy for rural laborers and their arduous lives in the Dutch countryside.
items.tags: peasant, rural life, dutch art, realism, early work, oil painting, 19th century
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: The Drinkers
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas depicts a group of figures engaged in drinking, reflecting a common social scene. The artwork showcases Vincent van Gogh's distinct style, characterized by bold brushstrokes and an expressive use of color.
items.tags: post-impressionism, figure study, social scene, expressive, drinking, dutch art
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Fishing in Spring, the Pont de Clichy (Asnières)
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's 'Fishing in Spring, the Pont de Clichy (Asnières)' captures a vibrant spring day along the Seine, featuring figures engaged in fishing near the iconic bridge. Executed in 1887, this oil on canvas work showcases Van Gogh's developing post-impressionist style through its energetic brushwork and vivid palette.
items.tags: fishing, river, landscape, spring, urban scene, post-impressionism, oil painting, france
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Madame Roulin Rocking the Cradle (La berceuse)
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's 'Madame Roulin Rocking the Cradle' portrays the subject in a vibrant, stylized manner, emphasizing the act of nurturing. Created in 1889, this oil painting captures an intimate moment of a woman rocking a cradle.
items.tags: portrait, woman, motherhood, oil painting, post-impressionism, vibrant colors, arles period
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Terrace and Observation Deck at the Moulin de Blute-Fin, Montmartre
items.medium: Oil on canvas, mounted on pressboard
items.description_narrative: This early work by Vincent van Gogh captures the lively atmosphere of Montmartre, depicting the Terrace and Observation Deck at the Moulin de Blute-Fin. Through vibrant brushwork, the artist invites viewers to experience a specific moment in Parisian life.
items.tags: Vincent van Gogh, Montmartre, cityscape, oil painting, post-impressionist, 19th century
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Grapes, Lemons, Pears, and Apples
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's 'Grapes, Lemons, Pears, and Apples' is a vibrant still life, capturing an array of fruits with the artist's characteristic energetic brushwork. This oil on canvas work exemplifies his developing style through its bold colors and expressive texture.
items.tags: still life, fruit, post-impressionism, vibrant, oil painting, expressive, domestic

items.title: Weeping Tree
items.medium: Reed pen and black-brown ink, with black chalk on off-white wove paper
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's 'Weeping Tree' is a powerful drawing from 1889, rendered with reed pen and black-brown ink alongside black chalk. The expressive lines convey the tree's form with an intense, almost animated quality, characteristic of his distinctive draughtsmanship.
items.tags: tree, nature, expressive, ink drawing, post-impressionism, solitary, draughtsmanship

items.title: The Basket of Apples
items.description_narrative: Paul Cezanne's 'The Basket of Apples' presents a vibrant still life composition. It exemplifies his innovative approach to form and perspective, where objects often appear to be viewed from several angles simultaneously.
items.tags: still life, apples, post-impressionism, french art, oil painting, multiple perspectives, compositional study, modern art
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: The Bay of Marseille, Seen from L'Estaque
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne depicts the expansive Bay of Marseille from the vantage point of L'Estaque, a fishing village that served as a frequent subject in his work. Through his distinctive approach, the artist carefully constructs the scene, emphasizing underlying geometric forms and the solidity of natural structures.
items.tags: landscape, bay, coast, modern art, structured, post-impressionism, l'estaque, french art
items.credit_line: 1QFFkcktbe4rAg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Auvers, Panoramic View
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne's 'Auvers, Panoramic View' offers an expansive landscape, showcasing his distinctive method of structuring form and space through color and brushwork. Rendered with structured brushstrokes, the painting reflects Cézanne's meticulous study of nature and his innovative approach to depicting depth and volume.
items.tags: landscape, post-impressionism, oil painting, French art, nature, modern art, Auvers
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Madame Cezanne in a Yellow Chair
items.description_narrative: Paul Cezanne's portrait of his wife, Hortense Fiquet, presents her with a striking solidity as she sits in a yellow chair. Through his characteristic brushwork and geometric approach, Cezanne transforms the sitter into an enduring, monumental form.
items.tags: portrait, post-impressionism, oil painting, figure study, domestic scene, structural, modern art
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: The Vase of Tulips
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne’s "The Vase of Tulips" exemplifies his revolutionary approach to still life, deconstructing form and exploring the interplay of color. Through bold brushstrokes and simplified shapes, he transforms everyday objects into a study of perception and artistic structure.
items.tags: still life, flowers, tulips, Post-Impressionism, French art, oil painting, modern art
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: The Bathers
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne's 'The Bathers' presents an assembly of nude figures, often female, integrated within a monumental landscape setting. This work exemplifies his exploration of form, color, and spatial relationships, anticipating Cubism and abstract art.
items.tags: bathers, nude figures, landscape, post-impressionism, modern art, proto-cubism, monumental

items.title: The Plate of Apples
items.description_narrative: This painting exemplifies Paul Cézanne's innovative approach to still life, depicting a simple arrangement of fruit with deliberate brushstrokes and a complex interplay of color. Through these forms, Cézanne meticulously explores the volumetric and spatial relationships, challenging traditional perspective.
items.tags: still life, apples, post-impressionism, oil painting, fruit, modern art, French
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Bathers
items.description_narrative: Paul Cézanne repeatedly explored the theme of bathers, presenting nude figures integrated within a landscape setting. This work exemplifies his profound interest in structuring form and space through color, rather than traditional linear perspective.
items.tags: bathers, nudes, landscape, Post-Impressionism, French art, figure study, oil painting

items.title: Standing Bather, Seen from the Back
items.description_narrative: This painting depicts a standing bather viewed from behind, a recurring subject in Paul Cezanne's oeuvre. Cezanne often explored the human form as a structured element within his compositions.
items.tags: figure study, bather, post-impressionism, oil painting, human form, french art, modern art
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884
items.description_narrative: Georges Seurat's monumental oil on canvas, "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884," captures Parisians enjoying a leisurely afternoon on an island in the Seine. This iconic work is meticulously composed using the artist's groundbreaking pointillist technique, creating luminous color and form.
items.tags: sunday, leisure, park, pointillism, post-impressionism, Parisian life, serene, vibrant

items.title: Oil Sketch for "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884"
items.description_narrative: This oil sketch is a preparatory study for Georges Seurat's monumental painting, "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884." It demonstrates Seurat's early exploration of light, color, and composition for his iconic work.
items.tags: oil sketch, preparatory study, pointillism, neo-impressionism, french, 19th century, parisian life, leisure
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Final Study for "Bathers at Asnières"
items.description_narrative: This oil on panel serves as a key preparatory study for Georges Seurat's monumental painting, "Bathers at Asnières." It showcases Seurat's early exploration of form, light, and composition before his development of Pointillism.
items.tags: study, figures, landscape, oil painting, post-impressionist, preparatory, early modern
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: The Starry Night
items.description_narrative: A swirling, dynamic night sky over a quiet village, painted during Van Gogh's stay at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. It is one of the most recognized masterpieces in the history of Western art.
items.tags: night, sky, stars, village, post-impressionism, landscape

items.title: Sunflowers
items.description_narrative: One of two series of sunflower still lifes by Van Gogh. Painted in Arles to decorate the room of his friend Paul Gauguin, the vivid yellows and expressive brushwork make this among the most recognizable still-life paintings in art history.
items.tags: sunflowers, still life, yellow, vase, post-impressionism

items.title: Café Terrace at Night
items.description_narrative: A warmly lit café terrace on the Place du Forum in Arles, France, under a deep blue starry sky. One of Van Gogh's first paintings to feature his signature nocturnal sky, it contrasts the warm golden gaslight with the cool blues of the evening.
items.tags: cafe, night, stars, arles, post-impressionism, urban

items.title: Starry Night Over the Rhône
items.description_narrative: Painted at dusk along the riverbank at Arles, van Gogh set gaslit town lights and the stars of Ursa Major shimmering above the Rhône's rippling reflections. It was one of several night scenes he made the year before his more famous Starry Night.
items.tags: van gogh, arles, rhone river, night sky, stars, post-impressionism, reflections

items.title: Irises
items.description_narrative: Painted in the first week of van Gogh's stay at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy, this study of the garden's flowerbed bursts with twisting blue-violet blooms against orange marigolds. Van Gogh considered it a calming color study, though it is now among his most reproduced paintings.
items.tags: van gogh, irises, saint-remy, asylum garden, flowers, post-impressionism, color
items.credit_line: DgFVFAJo_30MeQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Wheatfield with Crows
items.description_narrative: A turbulent sky of dark crows sweeps over a golden wheatfield split by three diverging paths, painted in the last weeks of van Gogh's life at Auvers-sur-Oise. Its brooding palette and unresolved paths have long invited readings as a symbolic farewell.
items.tags: van gogh, wheatfield, crows, auvers, turbulent sky, post-impressionism

items.title: Mont Sainte-Victoire
items.description_narrative: Cezanne painted the limestone ridge near his home in Aix-en-Provence dozens of times, breaking its slopes and the valley below into faceted planes of color. These late views of the mountain are considered a crucial bridge between Post-Impressionism and Cubism.
items.tags: cezanne, mont sainte-victoire, provence, landscape, post-impressionism, aix

items.title: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
items.description_narrative: Painted in Tahiti as what Gauguin considered his testamentary masterpiece, this sweeping frieze moves from an infant at right to an old woman at left, tracing the arc of human life among lush, dreamlike foliage. Gauguin later said he attempted suicide shortly after completing it, lending the work legendary, elegiac weight.
items.tags: gauguin, tahiti, symbolism, life cycle, post-impressionism, allegory

items.title: Vision After the Sermon (Jacob Wrestling with the Angel)
items.description_narrative: Breton women in traditional dress witness a vermilion-ground vision of Jacob wrestling the angel after hearing a sermon, the biblical scene rendered as pure imagination rather than observed reality. Painted at Pont-Aven, it announced Gauguin's break from Impressionist naturalism toward Symbolist abstraction.
items.tags: gauguin, brittany, symbolism, pont-aven, post-impressionism, vision

items.title: The Potato Eaters
items.description_narrative: Painted in Nuenen before Van Gogh moved to Paris and lightened his palette, this dark, earth-toned scene of a peasant family sharing a meal was intended as a statement of solidarity with rural laborers. Van Gogh considered it the first major work of his career; it now hangs in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.credit_line: rQE6qmf9oVuKPA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Wheatfield with Cypresses
items.description_narrative: Painted near the asylum at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, this canvas pairs a wind-tossed wheatfield with dark flame-like cypress trees Van Gogh described as 'beautiful in line and proportion, like an Egyptian obelisk.' He made several versions of the composition; this one is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

items.title: The Yellow Christ
items.description_narrative: Gauguin painted this crucifixion scene in Brittany, basing the yellow wooden Christ figure on a polychrome sculpture in a nearby chapel and surrounding it with local peasant women in traditional dress. Its flattened forms and bold outlined color fields exemplify Gauguin's Synthetist style; it is held by the Albright-Knox Art Gallery in Buffalo.

items.title: Equestrienne (At the Cirque Fernando)
items.description_narrative: Toulouse-Lautrec painted a bareback rider performing in the ring at the Cirque Fernando in Montmartre, using a sharply cropped, elevated viewpoint that suggests the influence of Japanese prints and photography. The circus was one of several Montmartre entertainment venues, alongside cabarets and dance halls, that became signature subjects of his career.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Moulin de la Galette
items.description_narrative: Toulouse-Lautrec depicted patrons seated around the dance hall of the Moulin de la Galette in Montmartre, the same popular venue Renoir had painted more than a decade earlier, but rendered here with flatter forms, sharper outlines, and a cooler, more detached mood. The painting reflects Toulouse-Lautrec's early engagement with the cafés and dance halls that would define his mature work.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: At the Circus: The Bareback Rider (Au Cirque: Écuyère)
items.description_narrative: Toulouse-Lautrec painted this circus performer on vellum, a support he favored for its smooth surface and slight translucency, capturing a bareback rider mid-performance with rapid, calligraphic brushwork. The subject reflects his lifelong fascination with the circus as a site of spectacle and physical performance.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Mahana no atua (Day of the God)
items.description_narrative: Painted in Paris after Gauguin's first stay in Tahiti, this canvas combines invented Polynesian imagery with a central idol arranged around a pool that reflects the figures above in bands of flattened, unnaturalistic color. The painting exemplifies Gauguin's Symbolist ambition to evoke myth and spiritual mystery rather than record observed reality.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Arlésiennes (Mistral)
items.description_narrative: Gauguin painted this scene of women bundled against the wind in Arles during his brief, tumultuous stay with Vincent van Gogh in the south of France in late 1888. The flattened forms, dark outlines, and unconventional cropped viewpoint show Gauguin moving away from Impressionist naturalism toward the bolder, more decorative style he would carry to Tahiti.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Woman in Front of a Still Life by Cézanne
items.description_narrative: Gauguin painted his companion Juliette Huet seated before a still life by Paul Cézanne that he owned and treasured, a painting he later carried with him to Tahiti as one of his few possessions. The work reflects Gauguin's deep admiration for Cézanne, whom he considered one of the most important painters of his generation.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Bathers at Asnières
items.description_narrative: Working-class Parisians lounge and swim along the Seine at Asnières, bathed in flat, hazy summer light and rendered with Seurat's early experiments in broken brushwork. It was the artist's first large-scale Salon submission and a precursor to his masterpiece "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte."
items.tags: neo-impressionism, seine, leisure, pointillism precursor, national gallery london, working class
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: Boy in a Red Waistcoat
items.description_narrative: Cézanne painted this portrait of a local Italian model, Michelangelo di Rosa, in Provençal costume during four sessions in the late 1880s. It is one of several versions of the subject the artist produced, this one now held by the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
items.tags: portrait, red waistcoat, italian model, provence, national gallery of art

items.title: Flowing Water in the Woods
items.description_narrative: This late landscape depicts a stream cutting through dense woodland, a motif Cézanne explored around Aix-en-Provence in his final years. Loose, overlapping brushstrokes of green and blue dissolve the scene into interlocking planes of color and light.
items.tags: landscape, forest, stream, woodland, late period, provence

items.title: Still Life with Fruit
items.description_narrative: This still life arranges fruit on a tabletop, a subject Cézanne returned to throughout his career to study form, color, and composition. It is held by the National Gallery in Prague.
items.tags: still life, fruit, tabletop, prague, national gallery

items.title: Still Life with Blue Pot
items.description_narrative: One of Cézanne's late still lifes, this composition balances a blue pot against fruit and drapery in the artist's characteristic tilted, multi-perspective arrangement. It dates from the final years of his career, now in the J. Paul Getty Museum.
items.tags: still life, blue pot, drapery, late period, getty museum

items.title: Bibémus Quarry (1898-99)
items.description_narrative: Cézanne painted the abandoned ochre quarry at Bibémus, near Aix-en-Provence, repeatedly in his last decade, drawn to its blocky, geometric rock faces. This version, dated 1898-99, reduces the quarry walls to interlocking planes of orange and green.
items.tags: quarry, bibemus, provence, rock formations, late period, geometric landscape
items.credit_line: Google Art Project works from the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art

items.title: Young Italian Woman at a Table
items.description_narrative: This portrait shows a young Italian model seated at a table, her form built from broad, faceted patches of color typical of Cézanne's mature style. It is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: portrait, italian model, seated figure, metropolitan museum, late style
items.credit_line: MAFz12krbdE_tg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Still Life with Apples
items.description_narrative: In this celebrated still life, Cézanne arranged apples, a ginger jar, and drapery into a carefully structured composition that treats everyday objects as studies in volume and color. It is one of his best-known still lifes, now at the Museum of Modern Art.
items.tags: still life, apples, ginger jar, drapery, museum of modern art
items.credit_line: WAHFm9iO_SGeQg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Abandoned House near Aix-en-Provence
items.description_narrative: This landscape depicts a derelict farmhouse in the countryside near Aix-en-Provence, rendered in Cézanne's structural patchwork of brushstrokes. It is held by the Dallas Museum of Art.
items.tags: landscape, abandoned house, aix-en-provence, rural, dallas museum of art
items.credit_line: Dallas Museum of Art, online collection

items.title: Trees and House, Provence
items.description_narrative: This Provençal landscape sets a house among trees, built up through Cézanne's characteristic small, directional brushstrokes that flatten depth into interlocking planes. The painting reflects his sustained study of the countryside around his native Aix.
items.tags: landscape, trees, house, provence, rural architecture
items.credit_line: IAFWl3-k88JZ3g at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Seated Man
items.description_narrative: This late portrait shows a seated male figure rendered with the loose, structural brushwork Cézanne developed in his final years. Facial and bodily forms are simplified into broad planes of color.
items.tags: portrait, seated figure, late period, provence, figure study
items.credit_line: 2QFehjzwoGoRjw at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Still Life with Onions
items.description_narrative: Cézanne arranged onions, a wine bottle, and a draped cloth on a tilted tabletop in this late still life, using shifting perspective to animate the composition. It is held by the Musée d'Orsay in Paris.
items.tags: still life, onions, wine bottle, drapery, musee d'orsay
items.credit_line: 4gHsoRzcJ38BlQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Big Trees
items.description_narrative: Painted near the end of Cézanne's life, this landscape depicts towering trees whose trunks and foliage are broken into overlapping strokes of green and blue. It is held by the Courtauld Gallery in London.
items.tags: landscape, trees, forest, late period, courtauld gallery

items.title: Landscape near Melun
items.description_narrative: This landscape depicts the countryside around Melun, south of Paris, an area Cézanne painted during a stay away from Provence. The composition uses his developing method of constructive brushstrokes to organize trees and fields into structured planes.
items.tags: landscape, melun, countryside, ile-de-france, rural
items.credit_line: lgHnZhWcptH7Rg at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: View of the Château Noir
items.description_narrative: This late landscape shows the wooded grounds surrounding Château Noir, an isolated property near Aix-en-Provence that Cézanne used as a studio and painted repeatedly in his final years. It is held by the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
items.tags: landscape, chateau noir, provence, late period, national gallery of art
items.credit_line: DQGY1JtjyPvAyQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Large Bathers
items.description_narrative: Cézanne worked on this monumental composition of bathers in a landscape for years, arranging nude figures into a triangular, architectonic structure beneath overarching trees. It is one of three large-scale Bathers canvases from his final decade, now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
items.tags: bathers, nude figures, landscape, late period, philadelphia museum of art
items.credit_line: owGszazN_Evyvw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Still Life: Milk Jug and Fruit on a Table
items.description_narrative: This still life arranges a milk jug and fruit on a tabletop, built from Cézanne's characteristic faceted brushwork and shifting perspective. The composition reflects his sustained interest in the tension between flat pattern and three-dimensional form.
items.tags: still life, milk jug, fruit, tabletop, color planes
items.credit_line: uAEu57ynKdy6cA at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Hollow with Trees
items.description_narrative: This landscape depicts a wooded hollow, its trees and terrain broken into Cézanne's characteristic overlapping patches of green, ochre, and blue. It dates from the early 1890s, a period of intensive landscape work near his home in Provence.
items.tags: landscape, hollow, trees, provence, woodland

items.title: View of the Sea at L'Estaque
items.description_narrative: Painted from the hills above the Mediterranean fishing village of L'Estaque, this landscape sets pine trees and rocky terrain against a band of sea and sky. Cézanne painted L'Estaque often in the late 1870s, using its high vantage points to explore flattened, structured compositions.
items.tags: landscape, l'estaque, sea view, pines, mediterranean, provence

items.title: Bathers
items.description_narrative: This composition of nude bathers set in a landscape belongs to Cézanne's long-running series on the theme, which he developed from imagination and earlier studies rather than live models. The figures are arranged in a loosely triangular grouping typical of the series' middle period.
items.tags: bathers, nude figures, landscape, figure composition, series
items.credit_line: UAEXdcwYwPHV5w at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Card Players (multi-figure version)
items.description_narrative: This painting belongs to Cézanne's Card Players series, depicting Provençal peasants gathered around a table absorbed in their game. The larger, multi-figure compositions in the series were based on studies of workers at the family estate, Jas de Bouffan.
items.tags: card players, genre scene, peasants, provence, figure group

items.title: Winter Landscape, Giverny
items.description_narrative: This landscape captures bare trees and open ground under winter light, rendered through Cézanne's structural brushwork. It reflects his continuing landscape practice outside his usual Provençal terrain.
items.tags: landscape, winter, trees, bare branches, seasonal

items.title: Still Life: Sugar Bowl and Pears
items.description_narrative: This still life arranges a sugar bowl and pears on a draped tabletop, built from Cézanne's characteristic small, directional brushstrokes. It is held in the Fondation Louis Vuitton, Paris.
items.tags: still life, sugar bowl, pears, drapery, fondation louis vuitton

items.title: Madame Cézanne in Blue
items.description_narrative: This portrait depicts the artist's wife, Hortense Fiquet, seated and dressed in blue, one of nearly thirty portraits Cézanne painted of her over two decades. Her features are rendered with the same structural, planar brushwork he applied to landscapes and still lifes.
items.tags: portrait, madame cezanne, hortense fiquet, blue dress, family
items.credit_line: rQHy_QckFYI03A at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Terrace at the Garden at Les Lauves
items.description_narrative: Painted in the garden of Cézanne's final studio at Les Lauves, above Aix-en-Provence, this landscape captures the terrace and surrounding foliage in loose, late-style brushwork. It dates from the last years of his life, when the Les Lauves property was his primary painting ground.
items.tags: landscape, les lauves, garden, terrace, late period, aix-en-provence
items.credit_line: swHLND9wt1UzlQ at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Standing Male Bather; Puget's Atlas
items.description_narrative: This double-sided study combines a standing male bather with a sketch after a sculpted atlas figure by Pierre Puget, reflecting Cézanne's habit of studying both live models and classical and Baroque sculpture. It illustrates the working process behind his recurring bather compositions.
items.tags: bather, male nude, sculpture study, puget, figure drawing
items.credit_line: UAFdNolZp0zsCw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Card Players (The Metropolitan Museum of Art)
items.description_narrative: This canvas from Cézanne's Card Players series shows two Provençal peasants seated at a table, absorbed in their game. It is among the smaller, two-figure versions of the series and is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
items.tags: card players, genre scene, peasants, two figures, metropolitan museum

items.title: Chestnut Trees at Jas de Bouffan in Winter
items.description_narrative: This landscape depicts bare chestnut trees at Jas de Bouffan, the Cézanne family estate near Aix-en-Provence, in winter. The artist painted the estate's grounds and avenues repeatedly through the 1880s as a stable, familiar subject.
items.tags: landscape, chestnut trees, jas de bouffan, winter, aix-en-provence
items.credit_line: IQE2o8CN-L_Hjw at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Village Square
items.description_narrative: This early landscape depicts a village square, its buildings and open space organized through Cézanne's developing structural brushwork. It is held in the Barnes Foundation collection.
items.tags: landscape, village square, architecture, barnes foundation, early period

items.title: Gardanne
items.description_narrative: Cézanne painted the hill town of Gardanne, near Aix-en-Provence, repeatedly during the mid-1880s, drawn to its compact, geometric massing of rooftops and walls. This view reduces the town to blocks of ochre and grey against the sky.
items.tags: landscape, gardanne, hill town, provence, geometric composition

items.title: Landscape in Provence
items.description_narrative: This landscape captures the rolling terrain and vegetation of Provence, built from Cézanne's characteristic patchwork of directional brushstrokes. It reflects his sustained commitment to the region's light and topography.

items.title: Turn in the Road

items.title: The Bather

items.title: Gardanne (Horizontal View)
items.description_narrative: This horizontal view of the hill town of Gardanne stacks its rooftops and walls into a compact arrangement of geometric blocks. It is held in the Barnes Foundation collection.
items.tags: landscape, gardanne, hill town, provence, barnes foundation

items.title: Mont Sainte-Victoire (Study I)
items.description_narrative: This is one of roughly thirty views Cézanne painted of Mont Sainte-Victoire near Aix-en-Provence, reducing the mountain and surrounding countryside to geometric planes of color. The mountain became his central subject of the last decades of his life.
items.tags: mont sainte-victoire, landscape, provence, mountain, late period
items.credit_line: dgFm740uqOu5Cw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Mont Sainte-Victoire (Study II)
items.description_narrative: This view of Mont Sainte-Victoire, near Cézanne's home in Aix-en-Provence, treats the mountain and foreground terrain as interlocking planes of color. It belongs to his extended series on the subject, which he painted obsessively from the 1880s until his death.
items.tags: mont sainte-victoire, landscape, provence, mountain, series
items.credit_line: sgHnFanUtHKRBQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Bathers (Small Group)
items.description_narrative: This composition gathers a small group of bathers within a landscape setting, part of Cézanne's long-running series on the theme. The figures are structured with the same faceted brushwork he applied to his landscapes.
items.tags: bathers, nude figures, landscape, figure group, series
items.credit_line: QwHJjmBqKey0yg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Fields at Bellevue (second version)
items.description_narrative: This landscape depicts the agricultural fields around Bellevue, near Aix-en-Provence, structured through Cézanne's characteristic patchwork brushwork. It is a further study of the Bellevue farmland he painted in the early 1890s.
items.tags: landscape, bellevue, fields, provence, rural
items.credit_line: YQGijCcy_62wCQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Ginger Pot with Pomegranate and Pears
items.description_narrative: This still life pairs a ginger pot with a pomegranate and pears, balancing the vessel's dark, upright form against the warm-colored fruit. It reflects Cézanne's recurring use of the ginger jar in his still-life practice.
items.tags: still life, ginger pot, pomegranate, pears, tabletop
items.credit_line: iwEUaDqSZWy7vg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Landscape: Road with Trees in Rocky Terrain
items.description_narrative: This landscape follows a road through rocky, tree-lined terrain, structured through Cézanne's characteristic overlapping brushwork. It reflects his sustained study of the rugged countryside around Provence.
items.tags: landscape, road, trees, rocky terrain, provence
items.credit_line: 1QHHYmLBFgOI7w at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Mont Sainte-Victoire (Study III)
items.description_narrative: This is another of the roughly thirty views Cézanne painted of Mont Sainte-Victoire near Aix-en-Provence, part of the series that occupied him obsessively in his final decades. The mountain and surrounding land are reduced to broad, faceted planes of color.
items.tags: mont sainte-victoire, landscape, provence, mountain, late period
items.credit_line: kgF8wo7pt6bJsA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Seated Woman in Blue
items.description_narrative: This late portrait depicts a seated woman dressed in blue, her form built from the broad, structural brushwork Cézanne developed in his final years. It reflects his continuing focus on portraiture alongside landscape in his last decade.
items.tags: portrait, seated figure, blue dress, late period, figure study
items.credit_line: 1AG7I2MOyfdjdw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.description_narrative: This self-portrait shows Cézanne rendered with the small, directional brushstrokes he adopted under the influence of Impressionism in the early 1880s. It belongs to a long sequence of self-portraits he painted throughout his career.
items.tags: self-portrait, figure study, introspective, early impressionist period
items.credit_line: 7wF4HYRiej54YQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: The Garden at Les Lauves
items.description_narrative: Painted in the final year of Cézanne's life, this landscape depicts the garden of his studio at Les Lauves, above Aix-en-Provence. The loose, unfinished-looking brushwork is characteristic of his very last works.
items.tags: landscape, les lauves, garden, late period, aix-en-provence
items.credit_line: SAEhQn_adsPLfg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: On the Banks of a River
items.description_narrative: This landscape depicts trees and terrain along a riverbank, structured through Cézanne's rhythmic brushwork. It is held by the RISD Museum in Providence.
items.tags: landscape, riverbank, trees, risd museum, rural

items.title: Melting Snow, Fontainebleau
items.description_narrative: This landscape depicts melting snow among the rocks and trees of the Fontainebleau forest, capturing a rare wintry subject in Cézanne's landscape work. It is held by the Museum of Modern Art in New York.
items.tags: landscape, snow, fontainebleau, forest, museum of modern art

items.title: Riverbank
items.description_narrative: This landscape depicts trees and terrain along a riverbank, structured through Cézanne's characteristic overlapping brushwork. It is held by the National Galleries of Scotland.
items.tags: landscape, riverbank, trees, national galleries of scotland

items.title: The Bend in the Road
items.description_narrative: This late landscape follows a road curving through terrain, its trees and embankments reduced to broad planes of color typical of Cézanne's final years. It is held by the National Galleries of Scotland.
items.tags: landscape, road, bend, late period, national galleries of scotland

items.title: Still Life with Teapot
items.description_narrative: This still life centers on a teapot among fruit and tableware, arranged with Cézanne's characteristic tilted perspective. It is held by Amgueddfa Cymru, the National Museum of Wales.
items.tags: still life, teapot, fruit, tabletop, national museum wales
items.credit_line: This image is uploaded as image number 2368 at Amgueddfa Cymru Images.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: At the Water's Edge
items.description_narrative: This landscape depicts trees and terrain at the edge of water, structured through Cézanne's characteristic overlapping brushwork. It is held by the National Galleries of Scotland.
items.tags: landscape, water's edge, trees, national galleries of scotland

items.title: Portrait of Antoine Valabrègue (alternate version)
items.description_narrative: This portrait depicts the poet and critic Antoine Valabrègue, a childhood friend of Cézanne's from Aix-en-Provence, painted with the thick, dark impasto typical of his early period. Valabrègue was part of the circle of friends who supported Cézanne's early career.
items.tags: portrait, antoine valabregue, friend, aix-en-provence, early period
items.credit_line: 1. J. Rewald, The Paintings of Paul Cézanne: A Catalogue Raisonné2. National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.

items.title: Harlequin
items.description_narrative: This portrait depicts a costumed figure of Harlequin, likely modeled on Cézanne's son Paul, part of a group of paintings related to a commedia dell'arte theme he explored in the late 1880s. It is held by the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
items.tags: portrait, harlequin, costume figure, commedia dell'arte, national gallery of art
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: The Road, the Old Wall
items.description_narrative: This early landscape depicts a road running alongside an old stone wall, structured through Cézanne's developing method of constructive brushwork. It is held by the Auckland Art Gallery in New Zealand.
items.tags: landscape, road, old wall, early period, auckland art gallery

items.title: The Bathers
items.description_narrative: This early composition of bathers gathers nude female figures in a landscape setting, part of Cézanne's long engagement with the theme across his career. The grouping and handling reflect the simpler, more Impressionist-influenced style of his earlier bather works.
items.tags: bathers, nude figures, landscape, early period, figure composition

items.title: The Bedroom (Amsterdam version, 1888)
items.description_narrative: The first of three versions van Gogh painted of his bedroom in the Yellow House in Arles, using flat planes of color to express restfulness. This original canvas is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: bedroom, yellow house, arles, interior, van gogh museum

items.title: The Bedroom (Musée d'Orsay version, 1889)
items.description_narrative: The third and smallest of van Gogh's three bedroom paintings, made as a gift for his mother and sister while he was a patient at Saint-Rémy. It is held today at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
items.tags: bedroom, arles, interior, musee d'orsay, repose
items.credit_line: C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition: image page

items.title: The Viaduct at Arles ("The Blue Train")
items.description_narrative: A steam train crosses a stone railway viaduct on the edge of Arles in this early Provence landscape, later nicknamed 'The Blue Train.' The painting is held at the Musée Rodin, Paris.
items.tags: viaduct, train, arles, railway, landscape, provence
items.credit_line: Cropped from File:Le Train Bleu, by Vincent van Gogh, from C2RMF.jpg, originally C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition: image page

items.title: Farmhouse in Provence
items.description_narrative: A sunlit view of a thatched farmhouse and cultivated fields near Arles, painted during van Gogh's prolific first summer in Provence. It is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: farmhouse, provence, arles, fields, rural landscape

items.title: Two Poplars in the Alpilles near Saint-Rémy
items.description_narrative: Two tall poplar trees stand against the hills of the Alpilles range near the asylum at Saint-Rémy, rendered in van Gogh's characteristic rhythmic brushwork. The painting is in the collection of the Cleveland Museum of Art.
items.tags: poplars, alpilles, saint-remy, trees, landscape

items.title: The White House at Night
items.description_narrative: A glowing yellow-lit cottage stands beneath a starry night sky in this late work from van Gogh's final weeks in Auvers-sur-Oise. It is held by the State Hermitage Museum, St. Petersburg.
items.tags: night, house, stars, auvers-sur-oise, nocturne

items.title: Portrait of Adeline Ravoux
items.description_narrative: A portrait of the teenage daughter of the innkeepers at the Auberge Ravoux in Auvers-sur-Oise, where van Gogh lodged during the final months of his life. It is held by the Cleveland Museum of Art.
items.tags: portrait, adeline ravoux, auvers-sur-oise, cleveland museum

items.title: Spectators in the Arena at Arles
items.description_narrative: A crowded scene of townspeople watching a bullfight in the ancient Roman amphitheater at Arles, capturing van Gogh's interest in local public life. The painting is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
items.tags: arena, arles, bullfight, crowd, roman amphitheater
items.credit_line: The Museum of Modern Western Art, Inv. Nr. GMNZI: 34

items.title: Basket of Sprouting Hyacinth Bulbs
items.description_narrative: A still life of hyacinth bulbs sprouting in a wicker basket, painted in Paris as part of a series of flower and bulb studies. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: still life, hyacinth bulbs, basket, paris period, van gogh museum

items.title: Bridge in the Rain (after Hiroshige)
items.description_narrative: A close copy in oil of Hiroshige's woodblock print 'Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge,' reflecting van Gogh's fascination with Japanese prints. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: bridge, rain, hiroshige, japonisme, van gogh museum

items.title: Still Life with Basket of Potatoes (I)
items.description_narrative: One of a group of similar potato-basket still lifes van Gogh painted in Nuenen as tonal studies in browns and earth colors. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: still life, potatoes, basket, nuenen, van gogh museum

items.title: Still Life with Basket of Potatoes (II)
items.description_narrative: A closely related second study from the same Nuenen potato-basket series, exploring the same subject with subtle variations in composition. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: still life, potatoes, basket, nuenen, van gogh museum

items.title: Still Life with Beer Tankards
items.description_narrative: A modest still life of ceramic beer tankards, painted during van Gogh's early Nuenen period as he practiced rendering everyday objects in muted tones. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: still life, beer tankards, nuenen, ceramics, van gogh museum

items.title: Basket of Apples
items.description_narrative: A still life of apples heaped in a woven basket, one of several fruit studies van Gogh made while developing his still-life technique. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: still life, apples, basket, fruit, van gogh museum

items.title: Garden with Courting Couples: Square Saint-Pierre
items.description_narrative: A public garden in Montmartre filled with strolling couples, painted with the broken, Pointillist-influenced brushwork van Gogh adopted after arriving in Paris. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: garden, paris, montmartre, couples, van gogh museum

items.title: Almond Blossom
items.description_narrative: Painted to celebrate the birth of his nephew, this study of white almond blossoms against a blue sky was inspired by Japanese prints. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: almond blossom, japonisme, blue sky, van gogh museum

items.title: Basket of Crocus Bulbs
items.description_narrative: A still life of crocus bulbs sprouting in a basket, part of van Gogh's Paris-period series of studies on flower bulbs. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: still life, crocus bulbs, basket, paris period, van gogh museum

items.title: Terrace in the Luxembourg Gardens
items.description_narrative: A view of visitors relaxing on the terrace of Paris's Luxembourg Gardens, reflecting van Gogh's shift toward lighter color and looser brushwork after moving to the city. It is held by the Clark Art Institute, Williamstown.
items.tags: luxembourg gardens, paris, terrace, park, clark art institute

items.title: The Yellow House
items.description_narrative: A view of the house in Arles that van Gogh rented and hoped to turn into a studio and gathering place for fellow artists. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: yellow house, arles, street, studio, van gogh museum

items.title: Portrait of Dr. Gachet
items.description_narrative: A melancholic portrait of Dr. Paul Gachet, the homeopathic physician who cared for van Gogh in Auvers-sur-Oise during the final months of his life. This version is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
items.tags: portrait, dr gachet, auvers-sur-oise, musee d'orsay
items.credit_line: OQE_w8xp1TtbSw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Basket of Pansies
items.description_narrative: A still life of pansies arranged in a basket, part of van Gogh's series of flower studies from his Paris years. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: still life, pansies, basket, flowers, van gogh museum

items.title: Still Life with Baskets of Potatoes
items.description_narrative: A composition of multiple baskets of potatoes, a more elaborate variant on van Gogh's Nuenen potato still-life series. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: still life, potatoes, baskets, nuenen, van gogh museum

items.title: Bobbin Winder
items.description_narrative: A study of a wooden bobbin winder used by local weavers, painted while van Gogh lived among the weaving community in Nuenen. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: bobbin winder, weaving, nuenen, still life, van gogh museum

items.title: Sprig of Flowering Almond Blossom in a Glass
items.description_narrative: A small, intimate still life of a single blossoming almond branch set in a drinking glass, painted in Arles. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: almond blossom, still life, glass, arles, van gogh museum

items.title: Allotment with Sunflower
items.description_narrative: A view of a vegetable garden plot in Montmartre with a single sunflower rising among the rows, painted during van Gogh's Paris period. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: allotment, sunflower, montmartre, garden, van gogh museum

items.title: Seated Nude
items.description_narrative: A study of a seated female nude, made while van Gogh attended life-drawing classes at the Antwerp and Paris academies. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: nude, figure study, academy, paris, van gogh museum

items.title: Banks of the Seine with the Pont de Clichy in Spring
items.description_narrative: A view along the Seine river on the outskirts of Paris, painted with the light, broken brushwork van Gogh absorbed from the Impressionists. It is held by the Dallas Museum of Art.
items.tags: seine, river, pont de clichy, paris, dallas museum

items.title: A Woman Walking in a Garden
items.description_narrative: A solitary woman strolls through a flowering garden path in this Paris-period landscape, painted with short, dabbed brushstrokes typical of van Gogh's encounter with Impressionism.
items.tags: woman, garden, paris, path, flowers

items.title: Harvest in Provence
items.description_narrative: A sweeping view of wheat fields being harvested near Arles under the intense summer sun of Provence, part of van Gogh's prolific harvest-season painting campaign of 1888.
items.tags: harvest, wheat field, provence, arles, summer

items.title: Portrait of the Postman Joseph Roulin
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Joseph Roulin, the Arles postal worker who became one of van Gogh's closest friends and favorite portrait subjects. Van Gogh painted Roulin and his family repeatedly during his time in Arles.
items.tags: portrait, joseph roulin, postman, arles

items.title: Shoes
items.description_narrative: A still life of a worn pair of shoes, a subject van Gogh returned to several times as a meditation on labor and simplicity. This version dates from his Paris period.
items.tags: shoes, still life, paris, labor, simplicity

items.title: Wheat Field with View of Arles
items.description_narrative: A golden wheat field stretches toward the rooftops of Arles in the distance, painted during van Gogh's productive summer of 1888 and reflecting his growing confidence with expansive, flat landscapes.
items.tags: wheat field, arles, landscape, provence, harvest

items.title: Les Alyscamps
items.description_narrative: A tree-lined avenue through the ancient Roman necropolis of Les Alyscamps in Arles, painted during Paul Gauguin's visit when the two artists worked side by side on the same motif.
items.tags: les alyscamps, arles, avenue, autumn, gauguin

items.title: At Eternity's Gate (Sorrowing Old Man)
items.description_narrative: A grieving elderly man sits hunched with his face in his hands, a painted reworking of an earlier lithograph van Gogh made a decade before. It was completed at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum shortly before his death.
items.tags: sorrow, old man, asylum, saint-remy, despair

items.title: A Weaver's Cottage
items.description_narrative: An interior view of a weaver's cottage in Nuenen, where van Gogh spent months observing and painting local handloom weavers at work. It reflects his early interest in depicting peasant labor.
items.tags: weaver, cottage, nuenen, interior, peasant labor
items.credit_line: QQFPfLmlSNyRHQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Windmills on Montmartre
items.description_narrative: A view of the windmills that once crowned the Montmartre hill in Paris, painted soon after van Gogh's arrival in the city and showing him experimenting with a brighter Parisian palette.
items.tags: windmills, montmartre, paris, hilltop, cityscape
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture: Home page – Image

items.title: Daubigny's Garden
items.description_narrative: A view of the walled garden of the late landscape painter Charles-François Daubigny in Auvers-sur-Oise, whom van Gogh deeply admired. He painted this garden in several versions during the final weeks of his life.
items.tags: daubigny's garden, auvers-sur-oise, garden, late work

items.title: Sunset at Montmajour
items.description_narrative: A large landscape of scrubland near the ruined Montmajour Abbey outside Arles at dusk. Long dismissed as a copy, it was authenticated as an original van Gogh in 2013.
items.tags: sunset, montmajour, arles, landscape, dusk

items.title: Fishing Boats on the Beach at Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer
items.description_narrative: Brightly colored fishing boats rest on the beach at the Mediterranean fishing village of Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, which van Gogh visited for several days in June 1888. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: fishing boats, beach, saintes-maries-de-la-mer, van gogh museum
items.credit_line: Saint Louis Art Museum, online collection

items.title: Blossoming Chestnut Branches
items.description_narrative: A close study of white chestnut blossoms against green foliage, painted in Auvers-sur-Oise during van Gogh's final, prolific months. It is held by the Kunsthaus Zürich.
items.tags: chestnut blossom, still life, auvers-sur-oise, kunsthaus zurich

items.title: The Church at Auvers
items.description_narrative: A dramatically distorted view of the Gothic church in Auvers-sur-Oise beneath a deep blue sky, painted in the final weeks of van Gogh's life. It is held by the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
items.tags: church, auvers-sur-oise, blue sky, musee d'orsay
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture: Home page – Image

items.title: Acacia in Flower
items.description_narrative: A close study of blossoming acacia branches, one of several tree-branch studies van Gogh painted in his last year. It is held by the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.
items.tags: acacia, blossom, branch study, nationalmuseum

items.title: Sunflowers (Van Gogh Museum version)
items.description_narrative: One of van Gogh's celebrated series of sunflower still lifes painted to decorate the Yellow House in Arles. This repetition, catalogued F458, is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: sunflowers, still life, arles, yellow house, van gogh museum

items.title: A Pair of Shoes (Arles, 1888)
items.description_narrative: A still life of a worn pair of shoes, painted in Arles and thought to have been inspired by a pair belonging to a local peasant. It is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
items.tags: shoes, still life, arles, metropolitan museum

items.title: The Brothel (Le Lupanar)
items.description_narrative: A brightly colored, stage-like scene of women and clients in a brothel parlor, painted during van Gogh's time in Arles. It is held by the Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia.
items.tags: brothel, arles, figures, interior, barnes foundation

items.title: Still Life with Basket of Apples (dedicated to Lucien Pissarro)
items.description_narrative: A still life of apples in a basket that van Gogh dedicated and gave to Lucien Pissarro, son of the Impressionist painter Camille Pissarro, as a gesture of friendship. It dates from his Paris period.
items.tags: still life, apples, basket, lucien pissarro, paris period

items.title: View of Saintes-Maries
items.description_narrative: A landscape view of the Mediterranean fishing village of Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, painted during van Gogh's brief seaside visit in June 1888.
items.tags: saintes-maries-de-la-mer, landscape, mediterranean, provence

items.title: A Meadow in the Mountains: Le Mas de Saint-Paul
items.description_narrative: A view of a meadow and tree with the Mont Gaussier rising behind it, painted near the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum grounds at Saint-Rémy during van Gogh's hospitalization.
items.tags: meadow, mont gaussier, saint-remy, mountains, landscape

items.title: Avenue of Poplars in Autumn
items.description_narrative: A woman walks along a tree-lined avenue carpeted with fallen autumn leaves in this early Nuenen landscape. It is held by the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
items.tags: avenue, poplars, autumn, nuenen, van gogh museum

items.title: Street in Saintes-Maries
items.description_narrative: A view of a simple street in the fishing village of Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, one of the works van Gogh made during his short stay there in June 1888.
items.tags: street, saintes-maries-de-la-mer, village, provence

items.title: Orchard with Blossoming Apricot Trees
items.description_narrative: A view of an orchard in bloom near Arles, part of a series of blossoming orchard paintings van Gogh made in the spring of 1888 while working quickly to capture the fleeting flowering season.
items.tags: orchard, apricot blossom, arles, spring, provence

items.title: Bowl with Peonies and Roses
items.description_narrative: A still life of peonies and roses arranged in a bowl, painted soon after van Gogh's arrival in Paris as he began experimenting with a brighter color palette. It is held by the Kröller-Müller Museum, Otterlo.
items.tags: still life, peonies, roses, bowl, kroller-muller museum

items.title: Wheat Field with Cypresses
items.description_narrative: A windswept wheat field with a dark cypress tree rising against a cloud-filled sky, painted at Saint-Rémy and considered by van Gogh one of his best summer canvases.
items.tags: wheat field, cypress, saint-remy, landscape, provence

items.title: At the Salon in the Rue des Moulins
items.description_narrative: This large canvas, held at the Musée Toulouse-Lautrec in Albi, shows women at a licensed Parisian brothel on the Rue des Moulins waiting in a salon between clients. Painted with unflinching, unsentimental observation, it is considered one of Toulouse-Lautrec's masterpieces of Parisian nightlife.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, brothel scene, Parisian nightlife, Post-Impressionism, Albi, genre painting

items.title: Horse Behind a Stable Gate
items.description_narrative: An early animal study by the teenage Toulouse-Lautrec, showing a horse standing behind a wooden stable gate. It reflects his lifelong fascination with horses, encouraged by his father and his early training under the equestrian painter René Princeteau.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, horse study, juvenilia, equestrian art, Albi, animal painting

items.title: Count Alphonse de Toulouse-Lautrec as a Falconer
items.description_narrative: A portrait of the artist's father, Count Alphonse de Toulouse-Lautrec, shown in traditional falconry dress with a hooded bird of prey. The elder Toulouse-Lautrec was an avid huntsman and eccentric aristocrat whose interests shaped his son's early exposure to horses and sporting life.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, falconry, aristocracy, family portrait, Albi

items.title: At the Moulin Rouge: Beginning of the Quadrille
items.description_narrative: This painting captures dancers assembling on the floor of the Moulin Rouge cabaret in Montmartre just before a quadrille begins. Toulouse-Lautrec was a habitué of the Moulin Rouge and became its de facto visual chronicler in the early 1890s.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, Moulin Rouge, cabaret, dance, Montmartre, nightlife
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

items.title: Alfred La Guigne
items.description_narrative: A portrait of a minor Montmartre figure nicknamed 'La Guigne' (bad luck), painted against a backdrop evoking the streets of Paris. The work exemplifies Toulouse-Lautrec's interest in the marginal characters of Montmartre nightlife.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, Montmartre, Paris, Post-Impressionism
items.credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

items.title: A Passing Conquest
items.description_narrative: Held at the Musée des Augustins in Toulouse, this painting depicts a fleeting romantic encounter, a theme consistent with Toulouse-Lautrec's candid scenes of Parisian social and sexual life in the 1890s.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, genre scene, Toulouse, Augustins, 1896

items.title: Young Horseman Mounting His Horse
items.description_narrative: An early equestrian scene painted by Toulouse-Lautrec at about age sixteen, showing a young rider swinging up onto his horse. It belongs to a large group of youthful horse and hunting studies now held at the Musée Toulouse-Lautrec, Albi.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, horse, equestrian, juvenilia, Albi

items.title: Portrait of François Gauzi
items.description_narrative: A portrait of François Gauzi, a fellow painter and close friend from Toulouse-Lautrec's student years at the studio of Fernand Cormon. Gauzi later wrote one of the first memoirs of the artist, documenting their shared life in Montmartre.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, friendship, Montmartre, Toulouse, Augustins

items.title: In Bed
items.description_narrative: Part of Toulouse-Lautrec's celebrated 'Au Lit' series painted from the brothels he frequented, this canvas shows a quiet, intimate moment between two women resting in bed. The series is notable for treating its subjects with sympathy rather than moral judgment.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, In Bed series, intimacy, brothel scenes, Albi, 1894

items.title: Carmen the Redhead (Carmen la Rousse)
items.description_narrative: A portrait of a red-haired model known as Carmen, painted early in Toulouse-Lautrec's career while he was studying in Montmartre. Carmen was one of several professional models the young artist favored for her striking coloring.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, model, redhead, Albi, 1885

items.title: Avenue at Céleyran
items.description_narrative: A landscape painted at Céleyran, the Toulouse-Lautrec family's country estate near Narbonne, where the artist spent many childhood and adolescent summers. The tree-lined avenue reflects his early training in outdoor observation before he turned to Parisian cabaret subjects.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, landscape, Céleyran, family estate, plein air

items.title: The Master of the Hunt
items.description_narrative: An early equestrian painting held by the Fondation Bemberg in Toulouse, depicting a huntsman in charge of the hounds and horses of a hunting party. It reflects the young Toulouse-Lautrec's immersion in the aristocratic hunting culture of his family.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, hunting scene, equestrian, Fondation Bemberg, Toulouse

items.title: The White Horse Gazelle
items.description_narrative: A study of a grey-white horse named Gazelle, one of many equine portraits Toulouse-Lautrec painted as a young man at Céleyran and Albi. Horses were a lifelong subject for the artist, whose physical disabilities limited his own riding but not his admiration for equestrian life.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, horse portrait, Gazelle, Albi, animal painting

items.title: Artilleryman Saddling His Horse
items.description_narrative: An early military and equestrian genre scene showing a French artillery soldier saddling his mount. Painted when Toulouse-Lautrec was about fifteen, it shows the technical skill in depicting horses that he developed under the tutelage of René Princeteau.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, military scene, horse, juvenilia, Albi

items.title: Horse in the Stable at Céleyran
items.description_narrative: A stable interior scene painted at the Toulouse-Lautrec family estate of Céleyran, showing a horse at rest. It is one of numerous equestrian studies the artist made on the estate during his adolescence.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, horse, stable, Céleyran, landscape

items.title: Study of a Woman, Nude from Behind
items.description_narrative: A half-length nude study of a woman seen from behind, part of Toulouse-Lautrec's extensive body of work depicting women in private, unposed moments. Such studies fed into his larger paintings of brothel and boudoir life in the 1890s.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, nude study, figure painting, Albi, 1896

items.title: At Her Toilette
items.description_narrative: A genre scene of a woman at her morning toilette, a subject Toulouse-Lautrec returned to often in the 1890s as part of his sympathetic depictions of women's private domestic routines. The painting is held at the Musée Toulouse-Lautrec, Albi.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, toilette scene, domestic genre, Albi, 1898

items.title: Portrait of Émile Bernard
items.description_narrative: A portrait of the painter Émile Bernard, a fellow avant-garde artist associated with Cloisonnism and a friend of Vincent van Gogh. The two artists crossed paths in the Parisian avant-garde circles of the mid-1880s.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, Émile Bernard, avant-garde, Paris
items.credit_line: Frey, Julia: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, BB art, Praha 1999

items.title: At the Moulin Rouge: Portrait of Monsieur Warner
items.description_narrative: A portrait of an English patron known as Monsieur Warner, shown at the Moulin Rouge, one of Toulouse-Lautrec's favored haunts for observing Parisian nightlife. The work is held at the Musée Toulouse-Lautrec, Albi.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, Moulin Rouge, nightlife, Albi, 1892

items.title: At the Moulin Rouge: The Dance
items.description_narrative: This large canvas shows dancers, including Toulouse-Lautrec's friend Valentin le Désossé, performing on the floor of the Moulin Rouge cabaret. It was one of the artist's first major paintings of the venue, painted around the time of the cabaret's own opening in the late 1880s.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, Moulin Rouge, dance, cabaret, Montmartre
items.credit_line: FAENd9LSU-ylzQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Portrait of Caudieux
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Caudieux, a popular café-concert performer of the Parisian entertainment circuit in the 1890s. Toulouse-Lautrec frequently painted and made posters of the singers and comedians who performed in Montmartre's cabarets.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, café-concert, performer, Montmartre, 1893

items.title: Crouching Woman (The Laundress)
items.description_narrative: A genre scene depicting a laundress crouched at her work, one of several paintings in which Toulouse-Lautrec turned his sympathetic eye toward Paris's working women. The subject reflects his broader interest in the everyday lives of women outside fashionable society.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, laundress, working women, genre painting, Albi, 1893

items.title: The Theatre Box
items.description_narrative: A scene set in a theatre box (loge), a subject Toulouse-Lautrec explored in several works capturing the social ritual of Parisian theatre-going. Such box scenes let him juxtapose fashionable spectators with the stage they had come to watch.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, theatre, loge, Parisian society, genre painting

items.title: At the Racecourse
items.description_narrative: A scene of the horse races, a fashionable Parisian pastime that combined Toulouse-Lautrec's twin interests in horses and modern urban leisure. The painting is held at the Musée Toulouse-Lautrec, Albi.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, horse racing, racecourse, leisure, Albi, 1881

items.title: Horse Behind a Picket Gate
items.description_narrative: Another of Toulouse-Lautrec's youthful horse studies made at Albi, showing a horse standing behind an open-slat picket gate. These studies, made in his teens, demonstrate the precocious observational skill that would later define his mature work.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, horse study, juvenilia, Albi, animal painting

items.title: The Clowness Cha-U-Kao
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Cha-U-Kao, a clown and acrobat who performed at the Moulin Rouge and the Nouveau Cirque, shown here in her distinctive yellow ruff and costume. Toulouse-Lautrec painted her several times as part of his fascination with the performers of Montmartre's demi-monde.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, Cha-U-Kao, clown, circus, Moulin Rouge, 1895
items.credit_line: tAEZCE0HugJzAQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Allegory: The Springtime of Life
items.description_narrative: An early allegorical composition by Toulouse-Lautrec depicting the springtime of life, a rare foray into idealized allegory before he turned decisively toward the realist observation of Parisian nightlife. It is held at the Musée Toulouse-Lautrec, Albi.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, allegory, early work, Albi, 1883

items.title: Horseman in Eighteenth-Century Costume
items.description_narrative: A costume study showing a horseman dressed in eighteenth-century attire, likely painted as an exercise in historical costume and equestrian pose. It belongs to Toulouse-Lautrec's youthful body of horse paintings at Albi.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, costume study, horse, historical dress, Albi, 1880

items.title: The Sofa (Le Divan)
items.description_narrative: A genre scene of two women seated together on a sofa, a subject drawn from the licensed brothels Toulouse-Lautrec frequented and painted with unusual tenderness. The painting is part of his broader series documenting the private lives of Parisian sex workers in the 1890s.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, brothel scene, sofa, intimacy, Post-Impressionism

items.title: Jane Avril Dancing
items.description_narrative: A portrait of the cabaret dancer Jane Avril in motion, one of Toulouse-Lautrec's favorite models and the subject of several of his most famous paintings and posters. Avril was known for her expressive, almost frenetic dancing style at the Moulin Rouge and the Jardin de Paris.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, Jane Avril, dance, Moulin Rouge, cabaret, 1892
items.credit_line: awEEswUy3gXkdg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: At the Cabaret
items.description_narrative: A scene set inside a Parisian cabaret, held today at the Musée de Libourne, capturing the informal sociability of the venues Toulouse-Lautrec frequented nightly. The painting reflects his enduring commitment to depicting entertainment life as he lived it.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, cabaret, nightlife, Libourne, 1898

items.title: English Soldier Smoking a Pipe
items.description_narrative: A portrait of an English soldier shown smoking a pipe, painted late in Toulouse-Lautrec's career. It reflects his continuing interest in individual character studies drawn from everyday encounters.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, soldier, Albi, 1898

items.title: View of the Vineyards at Céleyran
items.description_narrative: A landscape of the vineyards on the Toulouse-Lautrec family estate at Céleyran, painted during the artist's adolescence. Landscapes like this one predate his later focus on the enclosed, artificial world of Parisian cabarets.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, landscape, vineyard, Céleyran, 1880

items.title: By the River at Céleyran
items.description_narrative: A riverside landscape painted at Céleyran, part of a series of outdoor studies Toulouse-Lautrec made on his family's estate as a teenager. These early landscapes show a naturalistic technique quite different from the graphic, poster-influenced style of his mature Paris work.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, landscape, river, Céleyran, 1880

items.title: Rolande on the Sofa
items.description_narrative: A portrait of a woman identified as Rolande, reclining on a sofa, painted as part of Toulouse-Lautrec's series of intimate brothel interiors from the mid-1890s. The Musée Toulouse-Lautrec in Albi holds the work.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, brothel scene, Albi, 1894

items.title: Aristide Bruant on a Bicycle
items.description_narrative: A painting of the cabaret singer and songwriter Aristide Bruant, shown astride a bicycle. Bruant, known for his black cape and red scarf, was one of Toulouse-Lautrec's most frequent subjects and the star of several of his best-known posters.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, Aristide Bruant, cabaret, bicycle, portrait, 1892

items.title: Huntsman on Horseback
items.description_narrative: A hunting scene showing a mounted huntsman, part of the large body of equestrian and hunting subjects Toulouse-Lautrec painted in his youth at Albi. The work reflects the aristocratic sporting culture of his family.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, hunting scene, horse, Albi, equestrian

items.title: Clown
items.description_narrative: A study of a circus clown, reflecting Toulouse-Lautrec's early interest in performers and entertainers that would later expand to the cabaret dancers and singers of Montmartre. Painted in 1886, it predates his mature Moulin Rouge period by several years.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, clown, circus, performer, 1886

items.title: Artist with Green Gloves: The Singer Dolly
items.description_narrative: A portrait of the café-concert singer known as Dolly, who performed at the Star cabaret in Le Havre, shown wearing striking green gloves. Painted near the end of Toulouse-Lautrec's career, it reflects his continuing fascination with the personalities of the popular entertainment world.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, singer, Le Havre, café-concert

items.title: The Terrace at Château du Bosc
items.description_narrative: A view of the terrace at the Château du Bosc, the ancestral home of the Toulouse-Lautrec family in the Aveyron region. The artist spent considerable time there as a child and young man, and the estate appears in several of his early landscapes.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, landscape, Château du Bosc, family estate, 1880

items.title: Portrait of André Rivoire
items.description_narrative: A portrait of André Rivoire, a French poet and playwright who moved in the same literary and artistic circles of fin-de-siècle Paris as Toulouse-Lautrec. The painting is held at the Petit Palais, Musée des Beaux-Arts de la Ville de Paris.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, André Rivoire, Paris, Petit Palais

items.title: The Nun's Pines at Céleyran
items.description_narrative: A landscape at Céleyran depicting a stand of pine trees known locally as 'the nun's pines.' It is one of many outdoor studies Toulouse-Lautrec made on the family estate before dedicating himself to Parisian subjects.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, landscape, Céleyran, pine trees, 1880

items.title: The Black Countess
items.description_narrative: An early portrait, painted in oil on board, of a woman referred to as 'the Black Countess,' created when Toulouse-Lautrec was about seventeen. The painting is held at the Fogg Art Museum, Harvard University.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, early work, Fogg Art Museum, Harvard, 1881

items.title: Woman Seated in a Garden
items.description_narrative: An early outdoor portrait of a woman seated in a garden, reflecting Toulouse-Lautrec's youthful engagement with plein-air painting before he turned to the interiors of Parisian cabarets and brothels. The relaxed, naturalistic pose contrasts with the graphic stylization of his later work.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, garden, portrait, plein air, early work

items.title: The Ballet of Papa Chrysanthème
items.description_narrative: A painting related to the 1892 comic opera 'Madame Chrysanthème,' capturing a moment from its ballet sequence. Toulouse-Lautrec was closely tied to the Parisian theatre world and frequently painted scenes from contemporary stage productions.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, theatre, ballet, opera, Albi, 1892

items.title: At the Bastille: Jeanne Wenz
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Jeanne Wenz, sister of the painter Frédéric Wenz, shown near the Place de la Bastille in Paris. The painting is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, Jeanne Wenz, Bastille, Paris, NGA
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: La Goulue and Her Sister
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Louise Weber, the famous cancan dancer known as La Goulue ('the Glutton'), shown with her sister. La Goulue was one of the star performers of the Moulin Rouge and a favorite subject of Toulouse-Lautrec's paintings and posters.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, La Goulue, cancan, Moulin Rouge, portrait, NGA
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: Portrait of Maxime Dethomas
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Maxime Dethomas, an illustrator and stage designer who was a close friend of Toulouse-Lautrec in the artistic circles of Montmartre and later of the Opéra de Paris. The painting is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, portrait, Maxime Dethomas, friendship, NGA, 1896
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: The Artist's Dog, Flèche
items.description_narrative: A portrait of Toulouse-Lautrec's own dog, Flèche, painted in his youth. It is one of the earliest surviving examples of his affectionate, closely observed animal portraiture.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, dog, pet portrait, animal painting, NGA
items.credit_line: This file was donated to Wikimedia Commons as part of a project by the National Gallery of Art. Please see the Gallery's Open Access Policy.

items.title: Horsewoman (Amazone)
items.description_narrative: A study of a horsewoman riding side-saddle, a traditional equestrian pose for women of the period known in French as 'en amazone.' The painting belongs to Toulouse-Lautrec's extensive youthful catalogue of equestrian subjects at Albi.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, horsewoman, equestrian, Albi, 1881

items.title: The Jockeys
items.description_narrative: A painting of jockeys at the racecourse, combining Toulouse-Lautrec's early love of horses with the modern spectacle of organized horse racing. The work is held at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, jockeys, horse racing, Montreal, 1882

items.title: In Bed: The Kiss
items.description_narrative: A painting from Toulouse-Lautrec's 'Au Lit' series showing two women sharing a kiss in bed, one of the most tender and intimate images in his body of work. Unlike much contemporary genre painting, the series avoids sensationalism, presenting its subjects with quiet sympathy.
items.tags: Toulouse-Lautrec, In Bed series, intimacy, kiss, brothel scenes

items.title: The Bedroom
items.description_narrative: Vincent van Gogh's 'The Bedroom' depicts his living space in the 'Yellow House' in Arles, France. The painting features vibrant colors and a distinctive perspective, inviting viewers into the artist's personal world.
items.tags: interior, bedroom, post-impressionism, vibrant, personal, arles
